From the article, this is the entire article as the Kenosha News believes they own what happens in our town:

Nearly a year after Aaron Siler was fatally shot by a police officer, Kenosha County District Attorney Robert Zapf is ready to release his decision on whether Officer Pablo Torres was justified in his use of deadly force.

Zapf is expected to announce the decision Friday afternoon. Attorneys for Torres and Siler’s family are also expected to be at the news conference.

Torres, a Kenosha Police Department K-9 officer, has been on administrative leave since the shooting.

The March 14 incident took place on his first day back on the road after an earlier, non-fatal shooting that took place on March 4, 2015. Torres was found to have been justified in his use of force in the earlier matter.

Siler was shot in a garage off an alley near the 2100 block of 56th Street, following a car chase and foot pursuit. The chase started on 22nd Avenue, north of 35th Street, and continued south for 20 blocks.

Then, Siler turned onto 55th Street, driving onto the sidewalk, narrowly missing a house, skimming a tree and crashing into a parked car.

Siler, who had a felony warrant out for his arrest, then fled on foot, ending up behind Triple M Vending, 2103 56th St.

The Wisconsin Department of Justice Division of Criminal Investigations reviewed the Siler shooting, and submitted its findings to Zapf in August. The DOJ does not render any opinions, leaving that up to the district attorney. Zapf took that information, and hired a use of force expert, Emanuel Kapelsohn, to analyze the information.

This was a situation, Zapf said, with several factors that he felt needed an expert, outside analysis. He said Thursday that he had hoped to have a decision on this matter by the end of 2015, but without the expert report, was unable to issue his decision.

That report was turned in to Zapf late Tuesday afternoon. He said his decision will include a timeline that outlines why the investigation and decision-making process took as long as it did.

“I can assure you, there hasn’t been a day gone by where I haven’t been involved in and concerned with this case,” he said Thursday. “I take (homicide) cases extremely seriously. Even more so when there’s an officer involved.”
